name: Unnamed aerospace-and-defense placement with badge and PIV-card issuance

attribution.legal_posture: Official federal indictment; successful placement and badge/PIV-card facts remain allegations against the overseas worker

caveats: Behavioral signals require corroboration and human review; staffing, badge, device, download, location, and sector signals become DPRK attribution only with supporting evidence.
Official federal indictment; successful placement and badge/PIV-card facts remain allegations against the overseas worker.

statements: The indictment alleges a successful remote placement at an unnamed Fortune 500 aerospace-and-defense manufacturer through a staffing company. An employer laptop and PIV card were sent to the domestic laptop-farm address, and messages allegedly concerned retrieval of a physical badge by someone other than the represented identity.
defensive_controls: Require high-assurance identity continuity before issuing PIV/smart cards or physical badges to remote contractors.
Treat third-party retrieval of a badge, mail-forwarding address, or mismatch between badge holder and requestor as an escalation signal.
Bind staffing-company identity proofing to the end-client's own proofing rather than inheriting assurance by contract.
